title: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of the 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer's rich face, its first round at Study tier: three made pieces that each walk up to a test of their section's claim (the ratio gate, the symmetry-class morph rule, the RMS dip), and the bundle's renders, tours and étude gathered beside the sections they serve, with the fingerprint of the words each was laid against. I grow when the instrument is heard by hand and a piece has something new to test; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: The rational-ratio bullet says every output frequency is "a rational multiple of a common fundamental ω₂/q"; any frequency is a rational multiple of something, and that is not what makes it harmonic. The piece shows f = (m·p + n·q)·f₂/q: a whole-number multiple. Proposed: "a whole-number multiple of a common fundamental ω₂/q".

Units: with φ(t) = ω·t, ω is angular (radians per second), so f_mn = m·ω₁ + n·ω₂ reads as Hz only if ω means cycles per second. The piece writes φ = 2π·f·t and f = m·f₁ + n·f₂. Proposed: either say the scan rates are in Hz with φ = 2π·f·t, or write the spectrum as (m·ω₁ + n·ω₂)/2π.

The two bullets read as a binary gate; by the spectrum it is a slope, which is the Four Pillars claim. Measured on the piece's engine: the rational/irrational line is everywhere and inaudible (1.5 closes in 18.18 ms, 1.5005 = 3001/2000 in 18.2 s, 1.5 + 10⁻⁹ in 53 days, with the same spectrum); what moves is the detune δ = f₁ − (p/q)·f₂ from the nearest simple ratio. Each partial slides by m·δ (Penrose dragged 1.49 → 1.51: 45 lines, worst 0.010 Hz from m·f₁ + n·f₂) and partials that shared a harmonic beat at multiples of |q·f₁ − p·f₂| (Membrane at 112 : 110: the 330 Hz pair measured at 331.99 and 334.00 Hz). Proposed sentence after the bullets: "By ear the gate is not the line between rational and irrational, which is dense and inaudible, but the detune from the nearest simple ratio: each partial slides by m·δ, and partials that shared a harmonic beat apart at |q·ω₁ − p·ω₂|, slowing to stillness as the ratio arrives."

The section credits the irrational-ratio gate with load-bearing work toward piano-style accumulating inharmonicity. The ratio-gate piece shows the gate alone moves each partial by m·δ: linear in the ripple's count, not the quadratic n·√(1 + B·n²) stretch the section starts from. The quadratic enters through the stiffness warp or the Stiff String surface (Architecture's "second inharmonicity layer"). Proposed: say the gate supplies a linear, surface-shaped detune and the quadratic accumulation comes from the B warp.

"Surfaces sharing a common symmetry can crossfade cleanly; surfaces with different symmetry classes need a different morph treatment" does not hold by level. Measured on the full 1024² tables (Rich face checks/mid-morph-direct.py): Membrane ↔ Chladni, both 4-fold, dips 3.14 dB at mid-morph under a height-map crossfade; Membrane ↔ Theta, the page's own cross-class example, 3.01 dB; Membrane ↔ Penrose, which share nothing, 3.01 dB. The law matters where lattices overlap with opposed phase: Theta ↔ Matérn (overlap 0.89) 6.47 dB height-map against 0.24 dB spectral; Matérn ↔ Fisher 4.17 against 0.56. Proposed: overlap and phase agreement, not point group, predict the dip; for pairs that share nothing an equal-power crossfade is the whole fix. This is the steward's cycle-7 finding, never folded in.

"Spectral-domain is the right tool for cross-symmetry surface morphs (Membrane ↔ Chladni)": the Surfaces list calls both 4-fold, so the pair is not cross-symmetry, and the spectral law gains it 0.27 dB (3.14 → 2.87 dB at mid-morph). The pair where spectral morphing earns its FFT is Theta ↔ Matérn (6.47 → 0.24 dB). Proposed: name Theta ↔ Matérn, or say "overlapping, opposed-phase pairs".

Measured from 00_test_diagnostic.wav, row by row: sine → rising saw bottoms 9.6 dB below the constant-RMS target at 55% of the segment (9.2 dB at the midpoint), so "~10 dB" holds; but the deepest dip in the table is rising saw → square, 11.7 dB below target at 36% (14.5 dB below the louder anchor), and when two anchors' levels differ the bottom of the dip moves off the midpoint. Proposed: "~10–12 dB for negatively correlated anchors (sine → rising saw 9.6 dB; rising saw → square, the deepest, 11.7 dB, a third of the way across)".

The first question asks whether to crossfade "c_mn coefficients in spectral space" or "W directly in spatial space", saying they sound different. A linear crossfade of the c_mn is the same thing as a crossfade of W, since the Fourier series is linear; they differ only when the spectral morph blends magnitudes and turns phases, as Tools/morph_surfaces.py does. Proposed: "crossfading the coefficients' magnitudes (phases turned the short way) in spectral space".

pieces.caption: The torus as a product of two circles: the familiar stack of single-cycle frames (waterfall, left) and the same data as a rectangle (right), whose opposite edges glue into the donut above.

pieces.file: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — the ratio gate.html
pieces.title: the ratio gate · five steps
pieces.caption: **Line or slope?** One circle (an ordinary 1D wavetable), then two, then the surface's lattice projected onto the scan direction, then a ratio no fraction names, and last the page's own question: drag the ratio through 3 ⁄ 2 and watch whether the partials jump or slide. Checked offline on the piece's own worklet: every predicted line m·f₁ + n·f₂ found in the rendered spectrum; across 1.49 to 1.51 the worst line sits 0.010 Hz from its prediction; Membrane's shared 330 Hz harmonic splits to exactly |f₁ − f₂| at 112 : 110.
pieces.near: The ratio ω₁/ω₂ is the primary inharmonicity gate

pieces.title: Penrose Lattice, six held ratios · scan_surface.py
pieces.caption: The X phasor at 110 Hz and the rows at 1, 2, 3 ⁄ 2, 4 ⁄ 3, φ and √2 times that, 2.5 s each: four closed knots, then two that never close. The ratios were read back from the file's spectrum, not from a note; in the page's convention, f₁ ⁄ f₂ is the inverse of each.
pieces.near: Detuning the ratio off rational opens a closed orbit

pieces.file: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — surfaces and morphs.html
pieces.title: surfaces and morphs · five steps
pieces.caption: **Does symmetry decide the morph?** Nine voices from one scanning rule, then each as its lattice, then two lattices overlaid, then a height-map crossfade, and last the section's closing claim tested on the pairs the page names. Measured on the full tables: Membrane ↔ Chladni, both 4-fold, dips 3.1 dB at mid-morph, the same as Membrane ↔ Theta, the page's own cross-class example (3.0 dB), and as a pair that shares nothing. Theta ↔ Matérn, whose lattices overlap with opposed phase, dips 6.5 dB under the height-map law and 0.2 dB under the spectral one.
pieces.near: A symmetric morph stack across these surfaces is constrained by point group

pieces.title: Theta → Matérn, height-map crossfade · cycle 7
pieces.caption: 8 s, the morph the steward's cycle 7 surfaced from September's workshop. Listen for the middle going thin.
pieces.near: A symmetric morph stack across these surfaces is constrained by point group

pieces.title: Theta → Matérn, spectral crossfade · cycle 7
pieces.caption: The same pair, magnitudes blended and phases turned: the middle keeps its body.

sections.heading: The Five Generating Logics — Authoring Methods

pieces.title: Penrose under the Kuramoto scan · below, at, above threshold
pieces.caption: The bifurcation the third logic promises, heard side by side: shimmer below the coupling threshold, hiccups at it, lock above. Rendered by Tools/kuramoto_scan.py; not yet heard by Loudon.
pieces.near: Replace the linear scan with coupled oscillator dynamics

pieces.title: the coupling ramp, plotted
pieces.caption: Coupling ramped from 0 to 1.6 Hz on Penrose at ratio 1.518, pulled to 3 ⁄ 2: the slip rate falls and the lock order and harmonicity jump together at 0.80 Hz. A snap, not a fade, where the linear scan's gate is a slope.
pieces.near: Replace the linear scan with coupled oscillator dynamics

pieces.title: the three hands on Penrose · 24 s
pieces.caption: Bend, shear and stir in turn on the locked 3 ⁄ 2 knot, then all three as it opens. Rendered offline by the browser engine; not yet heard by Loudon.

pieces.title: the hands tour, spectrogram
pieces.caption: The harmonic lines never bend while the knot is locked; only their weights move, until it opens at 21 s. The warp catalog's lesson, seen: on a closed orbit a hand reweights partials, it doesn't retune them.

pieces.title: the warp bank on Knot Shadow · 25 s
pieces.caption: Five baked warps crossfaded on the locked 3 ⁄ 2 knot: blur, aimed blur, rotation, plate ring, stiff ridge. In the rotation (10–15 s), listen past 22.5° as the scan falls onto the surface's dead line. Rendered offline; not yet heard by Loudon.
pieces.near: The bake-and-crossfade machinery is built too

pieces.title: the Hopf tour on Penrose · 20 s
pieces.caption: Start at the south pole: 0–5 s is the plain 1D wavetable at 440 Hz, longitude sweeping the rows. Then the climb up the sphere, catching and slipping through the 1 ⁄ 4, 1 ⁄ 3, 1 ⁄ 2 and 2 ⁄ 3 bands; parked just off 3 ⁄ 2 while coupling rises, snapping shut at 13.5 s; then the locked knot sliding. Rendered with the instrument's own engine; not yet heard by Loudon.
pieces.near: A first mapping is built as a browser instrument

pieces.title: the Hopf control surface · the cycle 7 study, as it was
pieces.caption: **Start at the south pole.** Drag the dot to the bottom of the sphere and press play: that point is the classic 1D wavetable synth, and longitude chooses the row. Then climb. Gathered as built, including its own note boxes, which keep nothing inside the face; the page says it has not been played in a real browser, and this is the first place it can be.
pieces.near: A first mapping is built as a browser instrument

pieces.file: 2D Torus Wavetable Synthesizer — rich — the RMS dip.html
pieces.title: the RMS dip · five steps
pieces.caption: **Where does the middle of a crossfade go?** Sine and rising saw alone, then crossfaded, then the inner product that sinks the middle (−1 ⁄ π), then the constant-RMS fix, and last the real diagnostic table, all 1024 rows measured. Sine → saw bottoms at 9.6 dB below the constant-RMS target, as the page says; the deepest dip in the table is rising saw → square, 11.7 dB, a third of the way across.
pieces.near: Linear sample-domain interpolation between dissimilar anchor waveforms

pieces.title: per-row RMS of the diagnostic · the catalog's plot
pieces.caption: The catalog's own plot of the dip, row by row: the two silence anchors fall to zero by design; the first two segments, sine → saw and saw → square, are the deep notches.
pieces.near: Linear sample-domain interpolation between dissimilar anchor waveforms

pieces.title: the diagnostic table, played straight
pieces.caption: The table's 1024 rows read one after another at 48 kHz: a 46.9 Hz buzz (48000 ⁄ 1024) whose shape walks all sixteen anchors in 21.8 s. The level sags between anchors.
pieces.near: Linear sample-domain interpolation between dissimilar anchor waveforms

pieces.title: the same table, constant-RMS
pieces.caption: Every row scaled to the straight line between its anchors' levels (checked: within 0.000 dB of the target). The sag is gone; the shapes are unchanged.
pieces.near: Linear sample-domain interpolation between dissimilar anchor waveforms
